sources.title: Cranial morphology and phylogenetic relationships of Amynodontidae
sources.author: Veine-Tonizzo, Tissier, Bukhsianidze, Vasilyan and Becker (2023)
sources.evidence: Read original article. Fig5 real UNISTRA.2015.0.1106 skull/CT multiview,10cm bar; Table3 premaxilla-occipital555mm, premaxilla-orbit160mm. Genus diagnosis includes strong canines, massive cheek arches, high orbit. Species synonym M.rex; other named species validity needs revision.
sources.rights: CC BY4.0 authors. Private reference page rendered unchanged; no scan mesh reused.

sources.title: Amynodontidae
sources.author: American Museum of Natural History; Victoria Healy
sources.evidence: True AMNH1496 skull viewed. Museum describes short limbs, long broad torso, high eyes and hornlessness.
sources.rights: AMNH/Healy copyright; private visual reference only.

sources.title: Metamynodon planifrons skeleton
sources.author: Henry Fairfield Osborn, historical photograph before1923
sources.evidence: Real mounted skeleton image inspected for body/limb/neck proportions and canine orientation; mount restoration and perspective not exact living anatomy or ruler.
sources.rights: Public domain in US per source; no texture or skeleton mesh reuse.

sources.title: Preliminary report of a Metamynodon skull from the Byram Formation
sources.author: Manning, Dockery and Schiebout (1985), Mississippi Geology6(2)
sources.evidence: Original MGS1493 report measures greatest skull length600mm and width342mm. Separate specimen, not used as UNISTRA measurements. Discusses high orbit and sex-related canine/crest differences.
sources.rights: Publisher/author rights retained; private research, no figure redistribution in public asset.

sources.title: The Rise of the Mammalia in North America, part II
sources.author: Henry Fairfield Osborn
sources.evidence: Original account of Amynodontidae skeletal discoveries explicitly describes four functional forefoot digits. Hindfoot three-digit plan also consistent with inspected skeleton and standard amynodont reconstruction.
